_comment: Search partitions for discovery. Two things matter here and both were
learned the hard way from eBay's API behaviour:
1. buyingOptions is set explicitly on every partition. Browse returns
FIXED_PRICE only by default, so omitting it silently produces a
Buy-It-Now-only dataset - the exact bias this tool measures.
2. categoryIds is deliberately EMPTY and should stay that way. It
narrows the Browse search, and every allow-list we built was too
narrow: the 22 sovereign-named leaves dropped 2,491 genuine
Australian Sydney half-sovereigns, and the whole Coins subtree
dropped them too, because world coins hang off a different root
on EBAY_GB. Filtering is done instead on the category ANCESTRY,
which every search result already carries - see
_newlyListed: One partition per series that asks for the NEWEST auctions and stops
after a single page. It exists because of a measurement, not a hunch:
over 1,637 auctions, the median gap between a seller listing one and
this tool first seeing it was 87.8 HOURS - more than half of a 7-day
auction - and only 5% were seen within an hour. A tool that never sees
an auction near its start cannot know what it opened at, which makes
the question worth asking (does opening low draw more bids and a higher
The reason for the lag is that a fresh 7-day auction sits deep in a
relevance-sorted result set and only surfaces as it nears its end. So
sorting by newlyListed is the whole fix.
Auctions only, because a starting price is an auction idea. No price
bands and one page: 200 newest listings an hour against roughly ten new
sovereigns an hour is ample headroom, and paging deeper would just
re-fetch what the other partitions already sweep. One call per series
